steps.title: Prepare Gene FASTA Files
steps.instruction: Create text files in FASTA format for each gene to be used (e.g., Pilargidae_12S.txt, Gastropods_ATP6.txt). Ensure organism names are identical across all genes and contain no spaces.

steps.title: Import Data into Mesquite
steps.instruction: Open Mesquite and create a new file with 'Make Character Matrix' checked and 'DNA Data' selected as the data type.

substeps.instruction: Drag a gene text file into the program and import as FASTA.
Click 'Don’t Adjust'.
Delete the default top empty taxa.

steps.title: Align Non-Protein-Coding Genes
steps.instruction: For non-protein-coding genes (12S, 16S) or nucleotide-only analyses, align sequences and export them.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to 'Matrix' -> 'Align Multiple Sequences' -> 'MUSCLE Align'.
Select 'No' for running on multiple threads and click okay.
Verify the alignment.
Export the file in phylip (DNA/RNA) format.
Repeat for all applicable genes.

steps.title: Prepare Protein-Coding Genes for Translation
steps.instruction: For analyses involving amino acids for protein-coding genes, create and duplicate nexus files to maintain both nucleotide and protein versions.

substeps.instruction: Create a nexus file (do not align yet) and save it.
Duplicate the file; name one as the nucleotide version (e.g., Gastropods_ATP6_NT.nex) and the other as the protein version (e.g., Gastropods_ATP6.nex or Gastropods_ATP6_AA.nex).

steps.title: Configure Genetic Code and Codons
steps.instruction: Set the correct genetic code and codon positions for the protein-coding gene file in Mesquite.

substeps.instruction: Select 'List & Manage Characters' from the 'Character Matrix' sidebar.
Select 'Columns' -> 'Current Genetic Codes' from the toolbar.
In the 'Genetic Code' tab, select 'Invertebrate Mitochondrial' (or the applicable code), ensuring the column is selected so all values change from 'Standard'.
Select 'Codon Position' -> 'Minimize Stop Codons', ensuring the column is selected so values change from 'N' to numbers 1-3.

steps.title: Translate DNA to Protein
steps.instruction: Convert the DNA sequence to an amino acid sequence.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Characters' -> 'Make New Matrix From' -> 'Translate DNA to Protein' and click 'OK'.
Review the new tab for stop codons (black with asterisks); identify sequences that may need removal if stop codons appear throughout rather than just at the ends.

steps.title: Clean Protein Sequences
steps.instruction: Remove interfering characters from the translated protein sequence to prepare for RaXML analysis.

substeps.instruction: Save the file to prevent data loss.
Navigate to the end of the sequences and delete any empty columns.
Delete all stop codons using the 'Select' tool or the 'Edit' tool (replacing '*' with '-'). Ensure all stop codons, including those in shorter sequences, are removed.

steps.title: Finalize Protein Alignment and Export
steps.instruction: Align the protein sequences and export them to phylip format.

substeps.instruction: Delete the original nucleotide character matrix from the sidebar by selecting 'Delete Matrix', leaving only the 'Protein Translation of Character Matrix' tab.
Navigate to 'Matrix' -> 'Align Multiple Sequences' -> 'MUSCLE Align', select 'No' for multiple threads, and click okay.
Delete any empty columns at the end of the alignment and save the file.
Export as a phylip (protein) file (e.g., Gastropods_ATP6_AA.phy).
Set 'Maximum length of taxon names' to a large value (e.g., 100 or 200).
If an export error occurs regarding character states (e.g., 'W/M/V/C'), use the 'Edit' tool to change the value to '?' and save before re-exporting.
Repeat for all protein-coding genes.

steps.title: Run RaXML Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform Maximum Likelihood phylogenetic analysis using the RaXML GUI.

substeps.instruction: Load all alignments (non-protein-coding nucleotide phylip files and protein-coding amino acid phylip files) using the 'ADD ALIGNMENT' feature.
Select 'RUN MODELTEST' for every gene added (e.g., 15 genes for a full mitogenome analysis).
Set analysis to 'ML + thorough bootstrap + consensus'.
Set 'Runs' to 10 and 'Reps.' to 100 (or higher).
Leave the outgroup blank and use the default seed.
Run the analysis and ensure the computer does not go to sleep during computation.

steps.title: Visualize Results in Figtree
steps.instruction: Convert the output file and visualize the tree with bootstrap support.

substeps.instruction: Locate the output file ending in '.support' and change the file extension to '.tre'.
Open the '.tre' file in Figtree.
Check 'Node Labels' and select 'labels' from the 'Display' drop-down menu to view bootstrap results.
